title: A school for girls
hookLine: at Ferozepur, Bibi Harnam Kaur and Bhai Takht Singh built a school for Sikh girls

lines: AN IDEA SOME CALLED A WASTE.
cards: Ferozepur, a town in the Punjab. A husband and wife have an idea that some of their neighbors think is a waste: a proper school for Sikh girls. Reading, writing, Gurbani, Punjabi, practical skills.
Not a few lessons at home, but a school, with teachers and a place to live. They don't have much money. They have a conviction, and a lot of stubbornness.
Their names are Bhai Takht Singh and Bibi Harnam Kaur.

teach.h: KANYA MAHAVIDYALA: A SCHOOL FOR GIRLS.
teach.b: First, the two of them. Takht Singh was a teacher and a man of the Singh Sabha reform. Harnam Kaur was his wife and partner in the work.
The school came to be called the Sikh Kanya Mahavidyala: kanya means girl, and a mahavidyala is a great school. Tradition remembers it starting small and growing, one family's trust at a time.
Second, how they kept it going.
The school ran on gifts, and the story told about Takht Singh is that he traveled and asked for support again and again, collecting for the girls.
Harnam Kaur cared for the students who lived there, teaching, cooking, mothering. A school is a building, but it's also a person who stays up when a child is sick. Third, the reason.
The reformers wanted Sikhs to know their own scripture and history, and that couldn't stop at the boys.
If mothers couldn't read Gurbani, how would the next generation learn it at home? Teaching girls was part of renewing the whole community. Fourth, the Gurus' words underneath.
In the Japji, Guru Nanak returns again and again to one word: suniai, by listening. By listening, he sings, sorrow and sin are washed away.
The hymn names no one who is barred from listening, and the Gurus' hymns speak to all who listen, women and men alike.
A school for girls simply took those hymns at their word.

how: Sikh communities run and support schools and colleges, many open to girls and boys alike, and the reform-era girls' school at Ferozepur is remembered as part of that story.

o: by seeing, a word for the Guru's glance
by listening, a refrain of the Japji
by speaking, a call to recite aloud

practice: Bring to mind a girl you know, a daughter, a niece, a student, a neighbor, or the girl you once were, or the one your mother was, and picture her with a book open in front of her.
Picture someone patient sitting beside her, helping with the hard part, and breathe with that picture. If you pray, keep her in mind with each Waheguru on the breath out.

wordCard.voice: Suniai, by listening: the Japji's refrain, by which sorrow and sin are washed away. The Sikh Kanya Mahavidyala at Ferozepur let girls read, learn and teach. Today's word.

orig.note: suniai: by listening; a refrain of Guru Nanak's Japji.

carryVoice: Your line: girls, learning. They built something you can't read: a generation of women who could. Day nine hundred seventy-two, done.
